K215 Lean: one derived-rule development for Thm and the restricted ThmK

KThmK re-proved 22 rules of TarskiDerived and TarskiLeibniz with the same proofs (deduction, syllogism, contraposition, double negation, case split, quantifier monotonicity, existential elimination from vacuity, atomic substitution, existential monotonicity). Those rules now hold for any theorem predicate T that is classical (the existing hC) and, for the quantifier ones, carries the new class Tarski.Rows (generalization, rho1-rho7, membership vacuity). Thm and ThmK are instances, KThmK keeps only its calculus, basis and the genuinely restricted variants (equality-free vacuity and existential elimination, reflexivity at the helper binder, quantifier-free Leibniz, specialization and alpha-renaming), and the two vacuity inductions share their implication and quantifier steps (vac_imp, vac_all). atom_subst_rev takes symmetry as a hypothesis so that both calculi pass their own.

Thm call sites are unchanged (T is inferred from hC); KEind222 now passes classical to the six shared rules it uses. TarskiDerived + TarskiLeibniz + KThmK + KEind222: 1,176 -> 1,114 lines; KThmK 320 -> 215. Checked one module at a time: TarskiDerived, TarskiLeibniz, KThmK (with TarskiClean, TarskiComplete, Lukasiewicz), KCode222, KEind222, KSeedModel222, DomRho8, KCodeDom; KThmK's axiom reports are unchanged.

Rocq proposal: one shared implication core for DomRho8 and CD222

rho8cd/rocq-proposal/shared-core/ is the Rocq counterpart of the Lean shared-basis proposal: DominatedCore.v (generic Section, any connective with a reflexive domination relation closed under insertion into either operand) derives the unrestricted row, composition, lifting, K, Peirce and S from modus ponens and the restricted rows, rendered from the 58-step six-goal derivation of 3a7a61ee97; DomRho8.v (natural codes, <=) and CD222.v (domination True over thm222) are thin instances with the maintained public names. The maintained DomRho8.v + CD222.v total 1,399 lines / 45,538 bytes; the three files 322 / 15,360.

Compiled one coqc at a time in the .build/215 tree (Rocq 9.1.0): DominatedCore, DomRho8, CD222 (each closed under the global context), then the maintained users Prop222, G222, Interp222, Complete222 and ThmDom. KProfileTC was a generated copy (generate_profile_tc.py) of six ProfileComposition lemmas restated for TransContainers, because their proofs read only the transitive half of the CP hypothesis Containers and the lower chain's tagged domain has no literal power containers. The six lemmas now take TransContainers (defined in ProfileComposition, with transContainers_of_containers as a two-line bridge), so one proof serves both: CompositionModel applies the bridge at its two call sites and KLowerEqv uses the lemmas directly. KProfileTC and its generator are deleted; the k225-formal README no longer lists them.

K215 Lean: one transfinite recursion for the cumulative and the G-hierarchies

TransRec re-proved InternalRank's recursion along the internal ordinals (approximations, their uniqueness, one-stage extension, gluing, existence, and the stage lemmas) with z ⊆ T replaced by z ∈ G T. InternalRank now proves it once for any relation R z T named by a formula (RDef) whose classes {z | R z T} are sets (RSets): RApprox, rapprox_unique/eq/dom/extend/glue/exists, rstage_exists, RStage with rstage_exists'/unique/spec/mono. The cumulative hierarchy is the instance R = Sub (IsV, isVF, nsat_isVF and the isV_* lemmas keep their statements; IsV is definitionally the old one) and TransRec's G-hierarchy the instance R z T = z ∈ G T (Approx, IsStage, isStageF, nsat_isStageF, stage_exists', stage_unique, stage_spec, stage_mono keep their statements). InternalRank's internal approx_* lemmas and TransRec's private copies are gone; nothing outside used them.

InternalRank + TransRec: 752 -> 561 lines. Proposal: one bisimulation quotient, CP/GIC through a QHyp adapter

The KQ1* modules are generated forks of the CP/GIC quotient modules re-run on KQHyp.QHyp, so the quotient and its Separation, Pairing, Union, Power, Replacement and collection proofs exist twice. This proposal makes the QHyp development the only one: QuotientModel.ofCPGIC derives all nine QHyp fields from an inhabited CP/GIC model, and the Quotient* modules state the KQ1 results at that structure under their original names and statements (Domain/mk/quotientMember as abbrevs, one-line wrappers otherwise). generate_kq1.py is retired.

Filed as a proposal, not production: phase 14's merge 6901b164d9 keeps KQ1Model/QuotientModel/generate_kq1.py at its checked bytes pending its own kernel check, so production is left there. The patch applies to current main (git apply --check): 14 files, +147 -748. +One implication derivation now serves both the numerical and unrestricted calculi. `DominatedImplication` exports K, Peirce and S alongside its existing unrestricted-row, composition and lifting theorems. `Lukasiewicz` instantiates the same proof with domination always true, preserving its old public types and the complete Tarski bridge. The exact machine and both endpoint statements are unchanged.
+
+The generic core and Lukasiewicz module shrink together from **42,454 bytes / 811 lines to 18,243 bytes / 401 lines**: **24,211 bytes and 410 lines fewer**. The 179-module endpoint's selected sources shrink from **2,129,439 to 2,105,228 bytes**. Its module count and the five additional decoder-prefix modules remain unchanged. The generic core itself grows by 423 bytes; core plus unchanged numerical adapter is now **16,826 bytes**, against 16,403 before this change. The saving comes from sharing the formerly separate unrestricted derivation.
+
+The source follows the [attributed upstream `3a7a61ee97` / `49e99c5b7c` development](../phase12/upstream-merge/README.md), with [independent mathematical/API review](source-peer/review.md). Its changed suffix derives composition, exchange, prefixing and S within the same 58 MP steps. Two single-use conclusions are inlined, leaving 56 private proof lemmas and six public conclusions. The proof uses only the stated implication, derivability, MP and domination fields; it adds no bottom, truth, injectivity or stronger order assumption. The six generic theorem reports are axiom-free.
+
+This realizes the shared-basis idea from [Sources 185 and 187](../../../../../../../../../SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/set-theory/zfc-closure-kernels/intake-213.md). The selected two-module layout is 164 bytes and 17 lines smaller than the held three-module adaptation, and introduces no new module. These are alternative implementations; their savings do not add together.
+
+Two incremental Lean checks pass, each with an observed outer exit of zero:
+
+| Scope | Fresh providers | Reused providers | Typed checks |
+| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
+| Primary: 184 project modules plus three API clients | 36, including 33 project modules | 151 exact phase-twelve providers | 20 API reports; two additional endpoint clients with ten reports |
+| Compatibility: 68 project modules plus two old clients | 16 | 53 current-primary providers and one phase-twelve `Dag254` | Ten old-client reports and five existing `WFTheory` reports |
+
+The scopes contain **199 distinct project modules**, not a fresh 199-module build. Changed-source descendants were recompiled even when a direct dependency's object bytes were unchanged. Every reused source, import, dependency object and raw compiler log was checked; all nine physical site batches retain their exact accepted bindings and all 6,176 outcomes.
+
+The API reports distinguish their assumptions precisely: the generic client's seven reports have no axioms; the numerical client's five reports use exactly `propext` and `Quot.sound`; the Lukasiewicz client's first seven reports have no axioms, while completeness retains exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Both unchanged endpoint clients retain their ten exact standard-axiom profiles. The old compatibility clients retain all ten prior profiles. Every API and endpoint audit has zero warnings. Primary project logs contain 20 preexisting warning occurrences (six in freshly compiled unchanged sources and fourteen reused); compatibility logs contain seven (one fresh and six reused). There were no proof-compiler failures.
+
+The maintained [producer successor](source-proposal/production/generate_dominated_implication_lean.py) reads pinned raw proof text and ancestry data without executing the supplied renderer. Its inference controls, four CLI modes and post-adoption default check pass; the numerical adapter remains byte-identical. [Adoption](integration/adoption.json) records the two compiled source writes, synchronized producer and derivation input, and the upstream research renderer retained as unexecuted data. Exact before-bytes remain alongside it, including the old producer/input pair. The two retired templates remain absent.
+
+[Root's actual review](integration/root-actual-review.json), [current-source binding](integration/current-review.json), [producer execution review](integration/producer-actual-review.json) and [canonical producer check](integration/canonical-producer-actual.json) bind the adopted bytes. The compact [Lean execution packet](lean/README.md) preserves both accepted runs and their saved reviews. It retains an initial reader failure caused by expecting `Classical.choice` in the compatibility model report, the exact two-axiom correction and the successful rechecks. The proof sources and compiler records were unchanged by that correction. The source proposal and ordinary review keep their original historical statuses.
+
+The [previous checkpoint](../phase12/README.md) remains an exact historical record. This checkpoint changes no machine, endpoint statement or Rocq production source and adds no axiom. It supplies neither an internal PA proof nor a minimum-proof-size claim. Semantic site-contract integration and primitive/return factoring remain separate work.

+/-!
+A representation-independent dominated implication theorem.
+
+`rho8 L a b c u` is Lukasiewicz's single axiom ((c → u) → a) → ((a → c) → (b → c)) of the
+implicational calculus; `Restricted` grants it only when `u` is below `a`. The 58-step
+condensed-detachment derivation of the unrestricted row, composition and
+prefixing from modus ponens and the restricted rows alone was first rendered by
+`Research/ZFC/k225-formal/rho8cd/generate_domrho8_cd.py --core` from `rho8cd/derivation_core.txt`

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Render DomRho8 (Lean and Rocq) from a condensed-detachment derivation.
+
+  python generate_domrho8_cd.py [--derivation derivation.txt] [--lean OUT.lean] [--rocq OUT.v]
+  python generate_domrho8_cd.py --derivation derivation_core.txt --core DominatedImplication.lean
+  python generate_domrho8_cd.py --derivation derivation_luk.txt --luk Lukasiewicz.lean
+  python generate_domrho8_cd.py --derivation derivation_luk.txt --rocq-cd CD222.v
+
+The derivation (found by the untrusted search in search/) lists formulas over
+implication `>`, the code `Z` = 0 (with Z > Z = Z) and variables a, b, ...  Line
+`i j k F [C]` says that F follows by modus ponens from major j and minor k, under
+side conditions C (`x<=y`).  Leaf -1 is truth `Z`; leaf -2 is the dominated row
+((a>b)>c)>((c>a)>(d>a)) [b<=c], i.e. `rho8 c d a b` with `b <= c`.  Lines
+`#GOAL i F` name the lemma proving each public statement (by default the last line,
+which must then generalize that row with no side condition).
+
+--core renders a derivation without truth (no leaf -1 and no Z) as the
+representation-independent DominatedImplication module: an arbitrary binary
+connective with a reflexive `below` relation closed under insertion into either
+operand.  Its goals are the row, composition ((a>b)>((b>c)>(a>c))) and
+prefixing ((a>b)>((c>a)>(c>b))).
+
+--luk renders a derivation from the unrestricted row (no side conditions, no
+truth) as the Lukasiewicz namespace of Lukasiewicz.lean: K, Peirce, S and, when
+the derivation has that goal, composition.  The rest of the file (the Tarski
+bridge after the namespace) is kept verbatim.  --rocq-cd renders the same
+derivation as the Rocq lane's CD222.v (thm_K, thm_P, thm_B, thm_S over thm222).
+
+Each step becomes one lemma.  The renderer recomputes the most general unifier,
+so the premises' instances are explicit and every `u <= a` is proved from
+`le_l`/`le_r` (u a literal subterm of a), `0 <= a`, or a hypothesis of the lemma.
+The kernels check every step; nothing here is trusted.
+"""
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path

+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+Z = -1
+
+
+# ---------- formulas: int >= 0 variable, Z, or (antecedent, consequent) ----------
+
+def parse(s):
+    pos = 0
+
+    def go():
+        nonlocal pos
+        c = s[pos]
+        pos += 1
+        if c == '(':
+            a = go()
+            assert s[pos] == '>'
+            pos += 1
+            b = go()
+            assert s[pos] == ')'
+            pos += 1
+            return (a, b)
+        return Z if c == 'Z' else ord(c) - ord('a')
+
+    t = go()
+    assert pos == len(s), s
+    return t
+
+
+def norm(t):
+    if isinstance(t, tuple):
+        a, b = norm(t[0]), norm(t[1])

+    return t
+
+
+def walk(t, s):
+    while isinstance(t, int) and t in s:

+    return t
+
+

+    t = walk(t, s)

+def unify(x, y, s):

+        if x == y:

+            s[x] = y
+        elif isinstance(y, int) and y >= 0 and not occurs(y, x, s):

+theorem rho8_all (a b c u : Nat) : T (Code254.rho8 a b c u) := {row}
+
+end
+#print axioms rho8_all

+ROCQ_HEAD = '''(** Dominated rho8 derives every rho8 instance.
+
+    [rho8 a b c u] is Lukasiewicz's single axiom ((c -> u) -> a) -> ((a -> c) -> (b -> c));
+    [DomImp] grants it only when [u <= a]. The {n} lemmas are the condensed-detachment
+    derivation of k225-formal/rho8cd/derivation.txt, rendered by generate_domrho8_cd.py
+    exactly as for the Lean DomRho8 (the search that found it is untrusted). *)
+From Stdlib Require Import Arith Lia.
+From K230L Require Import Codes230.
+
+Record DomImp (T : nat -> Prop) : Prop := {{
+  dtruth : T 0;
+  dmp : forall a b, T (wim a b) -> T a -> T b;
+  drho8 : forall a b c u, u <= a -> T (rho8 a b c u) }}.
+Arguments dtruth {{T}} _.
+Arguments dmp {{T}} _ _ _ _ _.
+Arguments drho8 {{T}} _ _ _ _ _ _.
+
+Lemma le_l {{u x}} y : u <= x -> u <= wim x y.
+Proof. intro H. unfold wim. pose proof (P_ge_l x y). lia. Qed.
+Lemma le_r {{u y}} x : u <= y -> u <= wim x y.
+Proof. intro H. unfold wim. pose proof (P_ge_r x y). lia. Qed.
+
+Section Derivation.
+Variable T : nat -> Prop.
+Variable h : DomImp T.
+Local Opaque wim.
+
+'''
+
+ROCQ_TAIL = '''(** Every rho8 instance follows from the dominated ones. *)
+Theorem rho8_all a b c u : T (rho8 a b c u).
+Proof. exact ({row}). Qed.
+
+End Derivation.
+Print Assumptions rho8_all.
+'''
+
+
+COMPOSITION = parse('((a>b)>((b>c)>(a>c)))')
+PREFIX = parse('((a>b)>((c>a)>(c>b)))')
+ROW_NAMES = ['c', 'u', 'a', 'b']       # rho8 a b c u = ((c > u) > a) > ((a > c) > (b > c))
+
+
+K = parse('(a>(b>a))')
+PEIRCE = parse('(((a>b)>a)>a)')
+S = parse('((a>(b>c))>((a>b)>(a>c)))')
+LUK_END = 'end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Lukasiewicz\n'

+def render(rows, goals, mode, keep=''):
+    syn = Syntax(mode)
+    lemmas, names = steps(rows, mode in ('core', 'luk', 'rocqcd'))
+    body = [syn.lemma(*s) for s in lemmas]
+    if mode == 'rocqcd':
+        need = [(K, ['p', 'q']), (PEIRCE, ['p', 'q']), (COMPOSITION, ['p', 'q', 'r']), (S, ['p', 'q', 'r'])]
+    elif mode == 'luk':
+        need = [(K, ['a', 'b']), (PEIRCE, ['a', 'b']), (S, ['a', 'b', 'c'])]
+        need += [(COMPOSITION, ['a', 'b', 'c'])] if any(g == COMPOSITION for _, g in goals) else []
+    else:
+        need = [(ROW, ROW_NAMES)] + ([(COMPOSITION, ['a', 'b', 'c']), (PREFIX, ['a', 'b', 'x'])] if mode == 'core' else [])

+        assert not rows[i][3], 'a public statement has no side condition'
+        use[goal] = '%s h %s' % (names[i], syn.instance(rows[i][2], goal, vnames)) if mode not in ('rocq', 'rocqcd') else \
+            '%s %s' % (names[i], syn.instance(rows[i][2], goal, vnames))
+    if mode == 'rocqcd':
+        return RCD_HEAD.format(n=len(body)) + '\n'.join(body) + '\n' + RCD_TAIL.format(
+            k=use[K], p=use[PEIRCE], b=use[COMPOSITION], s=use[S])
+    if mode == 'luk':
+        tail = LUK_TAIL.format(k=use[K], peirce=use[PEIRCE], s=use[S])
+        if COMPOSITION in use:
+            tail = tail.replace(LUK_S_DOC, LUK_COMPOSITION.format(composition=use[COMPOSITION]) + LUK_S_DOC)
+        return LUK_HEAD.format(n=len(body)) + '\n'.join(body) + '\n' + tail + keep
+    head, tail = {'lean': (LEAN_HEAD, LEAN_TAIL), 'rocq': (ROCQ_HEAD, ROCQ_TAIL), 'core': (CORE_HEAD, CORE_TAIL)}[mode]
+    return head.format(n=len(body)) + '\n'.join(body) + '\n' + tail.format(
+        row=use[ROW], composition=use.get(COMPOSITION), prefix=use.get(PREFIX))

+CORE_HEAD = '''import Init
+
+/-!
+A representation-independent dominated implication theorem.
+
+`rho8 L a b c u` is Lukasiewicz's single axiom ((c → u) → a) → ((a → c) → (b → c)) of the
+implicational calculus; `Restricted` grants it only when `u` is below `a`. The {n} lemmas
+below are one condensed-detachment derivation of the unrestricted row, composition and
+prefixing from modus ponens and the restricted rows alone, generated by
+`Research/ZFC/k225-formal/rho8cd/generate_domrho8_cd.py --core` from `rho8cd/derivation_core.txt`
+(found by the untrusted search in `rho8cd/search/`). Each side condition holds by reflexivity
+and insertion into an implication operand, or is a hypothesis of the lemma; no truth value,
+formula decoder, injectivity or transitivity is assumed.
+-/
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.DominatedImplication
+
+universe v
+
+structure Language (A : Type v) where
+  imp : A → A → A
+  below : A → A → Prop
+  refl : ∀ a, below a a
+  grow_left : ∀ {{u x : A}} (y : A), below u x → below u (imp x y)
+  grow_right : ∀ {{u y : A}} (x : A), below u y → below u (imp x y)
+
+def rho8 {{A : Type v}} (L : Language A) (a b c u : A) : A :=
+  L.imp (L.imp (L.imp c u) a) (L.imp (L.imp a c) (L.imp b c))
+
+structure Restricted {{A : Type v}} (L : Language A) (T : A → Prop) : Prop where
+  mp : ∀ {{a b : A}}, T (L.imp a b) → T a → T b
+  rho8 : ∀ a b c u : A, L.below u a → T (DominatedImplication.rho8 L a b c u)
+
+section
+variable {{A : Type v}} {{L : Language A}} {{T : A → Prop}}
+local notation "wim" => L.imp
+local infix:50 " ≼ " => L.below
+
+private theorem le_l {{u x : A}} (y : A) (h : u ≼ x) : u ≼ wim x y :=
+  L.grow_left y h
+private theorem le_r {{u y : A}} (x : A) (h : u ≼ y) : u ≼ wim x y :=
+  L.grow_right x h
+
+variable (h : Restricted L T)
+include h
+
+'''
+
+CORE_TAIL = '''/-- Restricted rows and modus ponens alone derive every unrestricted row. -/
+theorem rho8_all (a b c u : A) : T (rho8 L a b c u) :=
+  {row}
+
+theorem composition (a b c : A) :
+    T (L.imp (L.imp a b) (L.imp (L.imp b c) (L.imp a c))) :=
+  {composition}
+
+/-- A proved implication lifts under any antecedent. -/
+theorem lift_right {{a b : A}} (hab : T (L.imp a b)) (x : A) :
+    T (L.imp (L.imp x a) (L.imp x b)) :=
+  h.mp ({prefix}) hab
+
+end
+#print axioms rho8_all
+#print axioms composition
+#print axioms lift_right
+end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.DominatedImplication
+'''

+`rho8cd/derivation_luk.txt` and found by the untrusted search in `rho8cd/search/`,

+machine) that this module previously ported. No implication injectivity or
+assumption about falsity is used.

+relative to `NF.bot`. Thus `Tarski.classical` supplies both explicit hypotheses
+of the previously conditional `Tarski.completeness`, for any theory predicate `Ax`.

+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Lukasiewicz
+
+universe u
+variable {{α : Type u}}

+structure Implicational (imp : α → α → α) (T : α → Prop) : Prop where

+  rho8 : ∀ c u a b, T (imp (imp (imp c u) a) (imp (imp a c) (imp b c)))

+from pathlib import Path
+import hashlib,json,subprocess,time
+R=Path('/home/codex/.codex/worktrees/ec20/Proofs');P=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+D=R/'Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/k225-formal/verification/k215/simplification/phase13/lean'
+sha=lambda p:hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+files=['README.md','basis-reference.json','basis.py','packet.py','review_saved.py','execution.tar.gz','index.json','result.json'];before={n:sha(D/n) for n in files}
+command=['python3','-B',str(D/'review_saved.py'),'--basis-repo',str(R),'--repo',str(R),'--output',str(P/'root-saved-review.json')]
+assert not (P/'root-saved-review.json').exists();start=time.monotonic();rec={'command':command,'packet_before':before};code=1

+ proc=subprocess.run(command,cwd=R,capture_output=True,timeout=180);code=proc.returncode
+ (P/'root-saved.stdout.txt').write_bytes(proc.stdout);(P/'root-saved.stderr.txt').write_bytes(proc.stderr)
+ rec.update(exit_code=code,stdout_sha256=hashlib.sha256(proc.stdout).hexdigest(),stderr_sha256=hashlib.sha256(proc.stderr).hexdigest())

+# Phase 13 recorded Lean checks
+
+This packet records the shared generic implication core and its shorter classical-logic adapter. The primary selection contains 184 project modules (179 for the endpoint and five for the uniform decoder prefix), plus three API clients: 187 providers, with 36 fresh invocations and 151 exact phase-12 reuses. The two additional endpoint clients report the same ten named standard-axiom profiles. The API clients produce twenty reports: seven constructive generic reports, five numerical reports using `propext` and `Quot.sound`, and eight classical-adapter reports (seven constructive; completeness uses the three standard axioms). The generic core itself prints six constructive reports.
+
+The compatibility selection contains 68 project modules and two existing clients: 70 providers, with 16 fresh invocations, 53 current-primary reuses and one phase-12 reuse (`Dag254`). It retains ten client reports and five existing `WFTheory` reports. The combined project set contains 199 distinct modules. All nine physical-site batches retain their exact earlier source, object and log identities; they were not rebuilt in this iteration. Warning counts are computed from the selected logs and separated by fresh and reused origin.
+
+Five adopted files are checked separately from the historical compilation inputs: the generic core, `Lukasiewicz`, the maintained producer, its derivation data, and an attributed research renderer preserved as inert data. The two historical canonical before-inputs are the old maintained producer and derivation; their exact snapshots remain bound. No supplied renderer, new Rocq compilation, or changed machine is part of this packet.
+
+`execution.tar.gz` contains only source and record material. It retains complete selected ledgers, fresh command/source/log records, API and endpoint audit sources/logs, planning and actual receipts, and the five adoption boundaries. Exact predecessor material is referenced through the pinned local [phase-12 packet](../../phase12/lean/README.md), not copied as ancestor archives or compiled objects. The phase-12 reader is invoked in historical mode; optional current-source comparison applies only to phase 13. The collector rehashes all live current providers, basis inputs, audit objects, logs and explicit historical snapshots after validation. The saved reader validates the recorded hashes and does not claim to recreate those objects or rerun Lean.
+
+From a checkout containing the predecessor packets:
+
+```sh
+python3 -B review_saved.py --basis-repo /absolute/path/to/Proofs --repo /absolute/path/to/Proofs --output /tmp/phase13-saved-review.json
+```
+
+Omit `--repo` to review this historical source checkpoint without requiring current maintained sources to match. `basis.py` verifies the exact local predecessor reader and archive hashes before loading that maintained reader; no member of an evidence archive is executed. The collector and metadata controls are retained inside the archive as provenance. The preliminary source-only plan remains unchanged alongside the final preparation records.

+"""Resolve the exact local phase12 evidence; never execute archive members."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import hashlib, importlib.util, json, sys, tarfile
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+PIN = '66112698049384540650932c48b6780b8fe5be46a6d5f20ba375d48b8f569b67'
+digest = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+
+def load(repo):
+    raw = (HERE / 'basis-reference.json').read_bytes()
+    assert digest(raw) == PIN
+    ref = json.loads(raw)
+    directory = Path(repo) / ref['repository_relative_directory']
+    def pins():
+        found = {}
+        for name, pin in ref['files'].items():
+            path = directory / name
+            assert path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()
+            data = path.read_bytes()
+            assert len(data) == pin['bytes'] and digest(data) == pin['sha256']
+            found[name] = data
+        return found
+    files = pins()
+    modules = [('basis', 'basis.py'), ('packet', 'packet.py'), ('_phase12_reader', 'review_saved.py')]
+    old = {name: sys.modules.get(name) for name, _ in modules}
+    bytecode = sys.dont_write_bytecode
+    try:
+        sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
+        for name, filename in modules:
+            spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, directory / filename)
+            module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+            sys.modules[name] = module
+            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        # Reuse the ancestor already validated by the exact phase12 reader.
+        ancestor = []
+        original_load = sys.modules['basis'].load
+        def cached_load(path):
+            assert Path(path).resolve() == Path(repo).resolve()
+            if not ancestor:
+                ancestor.append(original_load(path))
+            return ancestor[0]
+        sys.modules['basis'].load = cached_load
+        checked = sys.modules['_phase12_reader'].review(directory, basis_repo=repo, repo=None)
+        assert checked['status'] == 'PASS_SAVED_PHASE12' and not checked['current_sources_checked']
+        assert len(ancestor) == 1
+        previous, _, helper = ancestor[0]
+        index = json.loads(files['index.json'])
+        members = {}
+        with tarfile.open(directory / 'execution.tar.gz', 'r:gz') as stream:
+            for item in stream:
+                sys.modules['packet'].safe(item.name)
+                assert item.isfile() and item.name not in members
+                data = stream.extractfile(item).read()
+                assert index[item.name] == {'sha256': digest(data), 'bytes': len(data)}
+                members[item.name] = data
+        assert helper.manifest(members) == index
+        data = {'member:' + name: value for name, value in members.items()}
+        for path, route in json.loads(members['path-map.json']).items():
+            value = (members if route['storage'] == 'packet' else previous)[route['key']]
+            assert digest(value) == route['sha256'] and len(value) == route['bytes']
+            data['path:' + path] = value
+        assert pins() == files
+        return data, checked, helper
+    finally:
+        sys.dont_write_bytecode = bytecode
+        for name, value in old.items():
+            if value is None:
+                sys.modules.pop(name, None)
+            else:
+                sys.modules[name] = value

The actual compiler log and frozen final map correctly report only `propext` and `Quot.sound` for that theorem.

It retains the existing positive two-axiom control and adds rejection of an extra `Classical.choice`. The successor controls passed 10 positive and 35 rejection cases; collection and saved review with current-source checking then both exited successfully.
+
+The archive retains the entire first helper/configuration freeze, controls, raw failed traceback and outer record. The successor source peer and successful publication execution records are adjacent. This was an overstrict publication-reader assertion; neither Lean run failed or was repeated. No producer or supplied renderer was rerun to repair it.

+"""Check phase13's saved evidence and pinned phase12 reference without Lean."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import argparse, json, tarfile
+import packet
+
+def review(directory, basis_repo, repo=None):
+ directory = Path(directory); summary = json.loads((directory/'result.json').read_text()); index = json.loads((directory/'index.json').read_text()); members = {}
+ assert summary['status'] == 'PASS_COLLECTED_PHASE13' and packet.sha(directory/'execution.tar.gz') == summary['archive_sha256'] and packet.sha(directory/'index.json') == summary['index_sha256']
+ with tarfile.open(directory/'execution.tar.gz', 'r:gz') as stream:
+  for item in stream:
+   packet.safe(item.name); assert item.isfile() and item.name not in members
+   data = stream.extractfile(item).read(); assert index[item.name] == {'sha256': packet.digest(data), 'bytes': len(data)}; members[item.name] = data
+ assert packet.manifest(members) == index and len(members) == summary['archive_members']
+ for name in ['basis.py', 'basis-reference.json', 'packet.py', 'review_saved.py', 'README.md']:
+  assert (directory/name).read_bytes() == members['review/'+name]
+ freeze = json.loads(members['review/freeze.json'])
+ assert freeze['status'] == 'FROZEN_PUBLICATION_HELPERS_NOT_EXECUTED'
+ for name, pin in freeze['files'].items(): assert packet.digest(members['review/'+name]) == pin
+ checked = packet.validate(members, basis_repo, current_repo=repo)
+ assert all(summary[k] == v for k, v in checked.items() if k not in {'status', 'current_sources_checked'})
+ post = json.loads(members['review/live-postcheck.json']); assert post == summary['live_postcheck'] and post['status'] == 'PASS_LIVE_POSTCHECK'
+ assert post['providers'] == {packet.MAIN: 187, packet.COMP: 70} and post['combined_project_sources'] == 199 and post['endpoint_audit_objects'] == 2
+ assert post['all_live_sources_objects_logs_dependencies_rehashed'] and post['absence_gates'] == 2
+ config = json.loads(members['review/config.json'])
+ assert post['historical_inputs'] == config['historical_inputs'] and post['current_adoptions'] == packet.ADOPTIONS
+ for root, label in [(packet.MAIN, 'execution'), (packet.COMP, 'compatibility')]:
+  before = json.loads(members[label+'/before.json']); assert post['before_input_counts'][root] == len(before['inputs'])
+ return {**checked, 'status': 'PASS_SAVED_PHASE13', 'archive_sha256': summary['archive_sha256'], 'archive_members': len(members), 'reviewer_sha256': packet.sha(__file__), 'validator_sha256': packet.sha(Path(__file__).with_name('packet.py'))}
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+ parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+ parser.add_argument('--packet', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
+ parser.add_argument('--basis-repo', type=Path, required=True); parser.add_argument('--repo', type=Path); parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
+ args = parser.parse_args(); assert not args.output.exists()
+ result = review(args.packet, args.basis_repo, args.repo); args.output.write_bytes(packet.dump(result)); print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

+# Upstream49: shared implication and import-cut review
+
+The upstream shared implication pair is a better next candidate than our held three-file phase13 prototype. It implements the same semantic sharing, but a genuinely different 58-step derivation absorbs the five additional MP steps used by our exchange/S extension. It preserves the current generic and unrestricted public interfaces and the complete Tarski bridge. This is an ordinary source review with an independent finite syntax diagnostic, not fresh Lean acceptance.
+
+The reviewed range is `437804fcdd5550fec6ece3b6073c616690d4625f` to `49e99c5b7cc6c2e164331961de28bad3904361fd`: four commits and ten changed paths. Drop's separate merge census supplies exact Git/current/input preservation bindings. I read the new generic proof, unrestricted adapter, complete research renderer, derivation and documentation, and the import-cut changes. No renderer, compiler or submitted code was run.
+
+## The shared proof
+
+The first31 private proofs agree with the current core. The changed suffix derives composition, exchange, prefixing and S within the same58 MP derivation; K and Peirce reuse the existing early schemas. The last commit inlines only the two goal lemmas with no dependent lemma: the unrestricted row and S. Composition remains a named private schema because later proofs use it. Thus the final file has56 private MP proofs, two public inlined MP proofs, and the existing one-MP lifting application. There are23 restricted-row uses.
+
+My independent strict free-constructor reader checks every private proof and all six public conclusions, including each side-condition proof. Its only relation rules are a declared hypothesis, reflexivity and insertion into the left/right operand. It accepts no truth element, numerical zero, implication collapse, injectivity, order transitivity or extra inference rule. All checks passed. This diagnostic does not replace Lean elaboration.
+
+`Language`, `rho8`, `Restricted`, `rho8_all`, `composition` and `lift_right` keep their current headers. New exports are `k`, `peirce` and `s`. The unrestricted adapter uses the relation `True`, with trivial reflexivity/growth and the exact rho8 argument order. The old `Lukasiewicz.Implicational`, K, Peirce, composition and S headers are unchanged. Its entire Tarski namespace tail is byte-identical, so explosion still uses the original rho6 and no stronger completeness or consistency statement is asserted.
+
+The upstream pair is18,243bytes/401lines versus42,454/811 for the current checked pair:24,211bytes/410lines fewer. Our held phase13 prototype is18,407/418 across three files, so upstream saves another164bytes/17lines and one module. The two shared-basis implementations are alternatives, not additive savings. An inert import overlay on checked phase12 remains179 endpoint providers and184 with the five prefix providers, with no new module or import cycle.
+
+## The import split
+
+Commit e066 adopts the smaller alternative cut. Its `ZFModelSemantics.models_ZF` has the exact statement/body already checked in current `ZFModels`; both use the original `ZFNative` namespace. Current phase12 additionally separates `WFModelCore`, keeps `InductiveAttempts` explicit, and cuts the L2 producer import to Code254. Replacing these with upstream's broader WFModel wrapper gives back dependencies. Importing both semantic-module versions could duplicate the same declaration. Preserve the checked phase12 split; this upstream cut provides no additional saving.
+
+## Producer and adoption boundary
+
+The supplied renderer is ordinary untrusted source generation. Its new core-only branch uses a goal's explicit MP premise instances when no lemma refers to that goal and exactly one requested public theorem uses it. That is a sound syntactic inlining for the actual six unguarded goals. The existing Lean kernel remains the arbiter. +import Init
+
+/-!
+A representation-independent dominated implication theorem.
+
+`rho8 L a b c u` is Lukasiewicz's single axiom ((c → u) → a) → ((a → c) → (b → c)) of the
+implicational calculus; `Restricted` grants it only when `u` is below `a`. The 56 lemmas
+below are one condensed-detachment derivation of the unrestricted row, composition and
+prefixing from modus ponens and the restricted rows alone, generated by
+`Research/ZFC/k225-formal/rho8cd/generate_domrho8_cd.py --core` from `rho8cd/derivation_core.txt`
+(found by the untrusted search in `rho8cd/search/`). Each side condition holds by reflexivity
+and insertion into an implication operand, or is a hypothesis of the lemma; no truth value,
+formula decoder, injectivity or transitivity is assumed.
+-/
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.DominatedImplication
+
+universe v
+
+structure Language (A : Type v) where
+  imp : A → A → A
+  below : A → A → Prop
+  refl : ∀ a, below a a
+  grow_left : ∀ {u x : A} (y : A), below u x → below u (imp x y)
+  grow_right : ∀ {u y : A} (x : A), below u y → below u (imp x y)
+
+def rho8 {A : Type v} (L : Language A) (a b c u : A) : A :=
+  L.imp (L.imp (L.imp c u) a) (L.imp (L.imp a c) (L.imp b c))
+
+structure Restricted {A : Type v} (L : Language A) (T : A → Prop) : Prop where
+  mp : ∀ {a b : A}, T (L.imp a b) → T a → T b
+  rho8 : ∀ a b c u : A, L.below u a → T (DominatedImplication.rho8 L a b c u)
+
+section
+variable {A : Type v} {L : Language A} {T : A → Prop}
+local notation "wim" => L.imp
+local infix:50 " ≼ " => L.below
+
+private theorem le_l {u x : A} (y : A) (h : u ≼ x) : u ≼ wim x y :=
+  L.grow_left y h
+private theorem le_r {u y : A} (x : A) (h : u ≼ y) : u ≼ wim x y :=
+  L.grow_right x h
+
+variable (h : Restricted L T)
+include h
+
+private theorem d1 (v0 v1 v2 v3 v4 : A) (hb0 : v3 ≼ v0) :
+    T (wim (wim (wim (wim v0 v1) (wim v2 v1)) (wim v1 v3)) (wim v4 (wim v1 v3))) :=
+  h.mp (h.rho8 (wim (wim v0 v1) (wim v2 v1)) v4 (wim v1 v3) v0 (le_l (wim v2 v1) (le_l v1 (L.refl _)))) (h.rho8 v0 v2 v1 v3 hb0)
+
+private theorem d2 (v0 v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 : A) (hb0 : v2 ≼ v3) :
+    T (wim (wim (wim v0 (wim v1 v2)) (wim (wim v3 v1) (wim v4 v1))) (wim v5 (wim (wim v3 v1) (wim v4 v1)))) :=
+  h.mp (h.rho8 (wim v0 (wim v1 v2)) v5 (wim (wim v3 v1) (wim v4 v1)) (wim v1 v2) (le_r v0 (L.refl _))) (d1 h v3 v1 v4 v2 v0 hb0)
+
+private theorem d3 (v0 v1 v2 v3 : A) :
+    T (wim v0 (wim (wim (wim v1 v2) v1) (wim v3 v1))) :=
+  h.mp (d2 h (wim v1 (wim v1 v2)) v1 v2 (wim v1 v2) v3 v0 (le_r v1 (L.refl _))) (h.rho8 (wim v1 v2) v3 v1 (wim v1 v2) (L.refl _))
+
+private theorem d4 (v0 v1 v2 : A) :

+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.TarskiComplete
+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.DominatedImplication
+
+/-!
+The classical implicational basis and the unconditional Tarski logic bridge.
+
+K, S, Peirce and composition follow from modus ponens and Lukasiewicz's single
+axiom rho8 ((c → u) → a) → ((a → c) → (b → c)) alone. They are the dominated
+core's theorems (`DominatedImplication`) for the domination relation that holds
+everywhere: then every row is a restricted row. The one condensed-detachment
+derivation behind them (`Research/ZFC/k225-formal/rho8cd/`) therefore serves both
+the dominated calculus and this unrestricted one. No implication injectivity or
+assumption about falsity is used.
+
+Ex falso additionally uses the original rho6, whose existential is defined
+relative to `NF.bot`. Thus `Tarski.classical` supplies both explicit hypotheses
+of the previously conditional `Tarski.completeness`, for any theory predicate `Ax`.
+
+This concerns the named syntax with primitive falsity. It does not identify
+that syntax with numerical machine codes, justify the runtime falsity
+alias, verify a theory bundle, or prove a binary machine consistency endpoint.
+-/
+
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Lukasiewicz
+
+universe u
+variable {α : Type u}
+
+/-- Only the actual implicational row and its inference rule. -/
+structure Implicational (imp : α → α → α) (T : α → Prop) : Prop where
+  mp : ∀ {a b}, T (imp a b) → T a → T b
+  rho8 : ∀ c u a b, T (imp (imp (imp c u) a) (imp (imp a c) (imp b c)))
+
+variable {imp : α → α → α} {T : α → Prop}
+
+/-- Domination that always holds: every row is a restricted row. -/
+private def everywhere (imp : α → α → α) : DominatedImplication.Language α where
+  imp := imp
+  below _ _ := True
+  refl _ := trivial
+  grow_left _ _ := trivial
+  grow_right _ _ := trivial
+
+private theorem restricted (h : Implicational imp T) :
+    DominatedImplication.Restricted (everywhere imp) T :=
+  ⟨h.mp, fun a b c u _ => h.rho8 c u a b⟩
+
+/-- K follows from rho8 alone. -/
+theorem k (h : Implicational imp T) (a b : α) : T (imp a (imp b a)) :=
+  DominatedImplication.k (restricted h) a b
+
+/-- Peirce follows from rho8 alone. -/
+theorem peirce (h : Implicational imp T) (a b : α) :
+    T (imp (imp (imp a b) a) a) := DominatedImplication.peirce (restricted h) a b
+
+/-- Implication composition. -/
+theorem composition (h : Implicational imp T) (a b c : α) :
+    T (imp (imp a b) (imp (imp b c) (imp a c))) := DominatedImplication.composition (restricted h) a b c
+
+/-- S follows from rho8 alone. -/
+theorem s (h : Implicational imp T) (a b c : α) :
+    T (imp (imp a (imp b c)) (imp (imp a b) (imp a c))) := DominatedImplication.s (restricted h) a b c
+
+end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Lukasiewicz
+
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Tarski
+
+open NF
+
+private theorem implicational (Ax : NF → Prop) :
+    Lukasiewicz.Implicational NF.imp (Thm Ax) where
+  mp := Thm.mp
+  rho8 := Thm.rho8
+
+/-- Ex falso uses K, S and the original rho6, not rho8 alone. -/
+theorem ex_falso {Ax : NF → Prop} (a : NF) : Thm Ax (imp bot a) := by
+  let x := all 0 (neg (all 0 a))
+  let e := ex 0 (all 0 a)
+  have hk := Lukasiewicz.k (implicational Ax)
+  have hs := Lukasiewicz.s (implicational Ax)
+  have hbe : Thm Ax (imp bot e) := hk bot x
+  have hbea : Thm Ax (imp bot (imp e a)) :=
+    .mp (hk (imp e a) bot) (.rho6 0 a)
+  exact .mp (.mp (hs bot e a) hbea) hbe
+
+/-- The required classical basis is derived from the actual Tarski rows. -/
+theorem classical (Ax : NF → Prop) : Kalmar.Classical NF.imp NF.bot (Thm Ax) where
+  mp := Thm.mp
+  k := Lukasiewicz.k (implicational Ax)
+  s := Lukasiewicz.s (implicational Ax)
+  peirce := Lukasiewicz.peirce (implicational Ax)
+  efq := ex_falso
+
+/-- Unconditional completeness for named formulas with primitive falsity. -/
+theorem complete {Ax : NF → Prop} (f : NF)
+    (hval : ∀ (D : Type) (mem : D → D → Prop),
+      (∀ a, Ax a → ∀ e : Nat → D, Sat mem e a) → ∀ e : Nat → D, Sat mem e f) :
+    Thm Ax f :=
+  completeness (classical Ax) (classical (fun _ => False)) f hval
+
+end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Tarski

+
+def subst(term, env):
+    return tuple(subst(x, env) for x in term) if isinstance(term, tuple) else env.get(term, term)
+
+class Reader:
+    def __init__(self, text, schemas, counts, facts=None):
+        self.ts = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9.]*|≼|[()]', text)
+        assert ''.join(self.ts) == re.sub(r'\s+', '', text), 'unsupported syntax'
+        self.i = 0
+        self.schemas, self.counts, self.facts = schemas, counts, facts or {}
+
+    def pop(self, want=None):
+        token = self.ts[self.i]
+        self.i += 1
+        assert want is None or token == want, (want, token)
+        return token
+
+    def group(self, parse):
+        if self.ts[self.i] == '(':
+            self.pop('(')
+            result = parse()
+            self.pop(')')
+            return result
+        return parse()
+
+    def term(self):
+        def atom():
+            name = self.pop()
+            if name in ('wim', 'L.imp'):
+                return imp(self.term(), self.term())
+            assert re.fullmatch(r'v\d+|[a-z]|_', name), name
+            return name
+        return self.group(atom)
+
+    def guard(self, expected):
+        def parse():
+            name = self.pop()
+            u, a = expected
+            if name == 'L.refl':
+                value = self.term()
+                assert u == a and (value == '_' or value == a)
+            elif name in ('le_l', 'le_r'):
+                other = self.term()
+                assert isinstance(a, tuple) and a[0] == 'imp'
+                fixed, grown = (2, 1) if name == 'le_l' else (1, 2)
+                assert a[fixed] == other
+                self.guard((u, a[grown]))
+            else:
+                assert self.facts[name] == expected
+        self.group(parse)
+
+    def proof(self):
+        def parse():
+            name = self.pop()
+            if name == 'h.mp':
+                major, minor = self.proof(), self.proof()
+                assert isinstance(major, tuple) and major[0] == 'imp'
+                assert major[1] == minor, ('MP mismatch', major, minor)
+                self.counts['mp'] += 1
+                return major[2]
+            if name == 'h.rho8':
+                a, b, c, u = [self.term() for _ in range(4)]
+                self.guard((u, a))
+                self.counts['restricted_rows'] += 1
+                return row(a, b, c, u)
+            if name in self.schemas:
+                self.pop('h')
+                args, target, guards = self.schemas[name]
+                env = dict(zip(args, [self.term() for _ in args]))
+                for guard in guards:
+                    self.guard(subst(guard, env))
+                return subst(target, env)
+            assert name in self.facts, name
+            return self.facts[name]
+        return self.group(parse)
+
+    def end(self):
+        assert self.i == len(self.ts), self.ts[self.i:]
+
+def audit(core, inlined=False):
+    schemas, counts = {}, {'mp': 0, 'restricted_rows': 0}
+    matches = list(re.finditer(r'private theorem (d\d+)\b', core))
+    expected = [f'd{i}' for i in range(1, 59) if not inlined or i not in (56, 58)]
+    assert [m.group(1) for m in matches] == expected
+    for index, match in enumerate(matches):
+        end = matches[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(matches) else core.index('/-- Restricted rows', match.end())
+        header, body = core[match.end():end].split(':=', 1)
+        args = [a for group in re.findall(r'\(([^():]+) : A\)', header) for a in group.split()]
+        facts, guards = {}, []
+        for name, text in re.findall(r'\((hb\d+) : (.*?)\)\s*:', header, re.S):
+            r = Reader(text, schemas, counts)
+            u = r.term(); r.pop('≼'); a = r.term(); r.end()
+            facts[name] = (u, a)
+            guards.append((u, a))
+        r = Reader(re.split(r':\s*T\s+', header)[-1], schemas, counts)
+        target = r.term(); r.end()
+        before = counts['mp']
+        r = Reader(body.strip(), schemas, counts, facts)
+        assert r.proof() == target, match.group(1)
+        r.end()
+        assert counts['mp'] == before + 1
+        schemas[match.group(1)] = (args, target, guards)
+    assert counts == {'mp': len(expected), 'restricted_rows': 23}
+    assert not re.search(r'WithSeed|h\.truth|\b0\b|Nat\.|sorry|native_decide', core)
+    assert not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*axiom\b', core)
+    targets = {
+        'rho8_all': row('a', 'b', 'c', 'u'),
+        'composition': imp(imp('a', 'b'), imp(imp('b', 'c'), imp('a', 'c'))),
+        'lift_right': imp(imp('x', 'a'), imp('x', 'b')),
+    }
+    public = list(re.finditer(r'(?m)^theorem (\w+)\b', core))
+    assert [m.group(1) for m in public] == list(targets)
+    for index, match in enumerate(public):
+        end = public[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(public) else core.index('\nend\n', match.end())
+        body = core[match.end():end].split(':=', 1)[1]
+        body = re.sub(r'/--.*?-/\s*$', '', body, flags=re.S).strip()
+        r = Reader(body, schemas, counts, {'hab': imp('a', 'b')})
+        assert r.proof() == targets[match.group(1)], match.group(1)
+        r.end()
+    assert counts == {'mp': 59, 'restricted_rows': 23}
+    return {'private_steps': len(expected), 'private_mp': len(expected), 'restricted_rows': 23,
+            'public_mp': 59 - len(expected), 'seed_uses': 0, 'public_targets': list(targets)}
+
+def render_core(raw_core):
+    core = raw_core
+    for name, args, pin in [
+        ('d56', ['c', 'u', 'a', 'b'], '4c5c289425be0a601f699f48b4ed5b9be91dc1fcc0684d9dabbc16e78200f753'),
+        ('d58', ['a', 'b', 'c'], 'd371f672d1b010dfe026b34443c53228f16864c5c7bd9cdacd84f10009f7cda4'),
+    ]:
+        match = re.search(r'private theorem ' + name + r'\b.*?(?=private theorem |/-- Restricted rows)', core, re.S)
+        block = match.group()
+        assert sha(block.encode()) == pin
+        env = {f'v{i}': a for i, a in enumerate(args)}
+        body = re.sub(r'\bv\d+\b', lambda m: env[m.group()], block.split(':=\n', 1)[1]).rstrip('\n')
+        core = core[:match.start()] + core[match.end():]
+        call = '  ' + name + ' h ' + ' '.join(args)
+        assert core.count(call) == 1 and len(re.findall(r'\b' + name + r'\b', core)) == 1
+        core = core.replace(call, body)
+    before = ('The 58 lemmas\nbelow are one condensed-detachment derivation of the unrestricted row, composition and\n'
+              'prefixing from modus ponens and the restricted rows alone, generated by')
+    after = ('The 58-step\ncondensed-detachment derivation of the unrestricted row, composition and\n'
+             'prefixing from modus ponens and the restricted rows alone was first rendered by')
+    assert core.count(before) == 1 and not re.search(r'\bd(?:56|58)\b', core)
+    return core.replace(before, after)
+
+def generate():
+    inputs = {}
+    for name, expected in INPUT_PINS.items():
+        raw = (HERE / name).read_bytes()
+        assert sha(raw) == expected, 'input bytes differ: ' + name
+        inputs[name] = raw.decode('utf-8')
+    raw_checked = audit(inputs[SOURCE])
+    core, adapter = render_core(inputs[SOURCE]), inputs[ADAPTER]
+    assert sha(core.encode()) == EXPECTED_CORE, 'output differs from reviewed core'
+    checked = audit(core, inlined=True)
+    metrics = {'input_raw_sha256': INPUT_PINS, 'generic_sha256': sha(core.encode()),
+               'adapter_sha256': sha(adapter.encode()), 'generic_bytes': len(core.encode()),
+               'adapter_bytes': len(adapter.encode()), 'combined_bytes': len((core + adapter).encode()),
+               'generic_lines': len(core.splitlines()), 'adapter_lines': len(adapter.splitlines()),
+               'raw_checked': raw_checked, 'checked': checked,
+               'derivation_role': 'Pinned ancestry data; no renderer execution.',
+               'kernel_status': 'External Lean receipts; this diagnostic is not a proof kernel.'}
+    return core, adapter, metrics
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, help='write repo-layout Lean files under this directory')
+    parser.add_argument('--check', action='store_true', help='check exact maintained source bytes')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    core, adapter, metrics = generate()
+    target = (args.out or DEFAULT_OUT) / 'BusyBeaver/ZFC'
+    outputs = {'DominatedImplication.lean': core, 'DomRho8.lean': adapter}
+    if args.check or args.out is None:
+        for name, text in outputs.items():
+            assert (target / name).read_bytes() == text.encode(), 'maintained source bytes differ: ' + name
+    else:
+        target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        for name, text in outputs.items():
+            (target / name).write_bytes(text.encode())
+        (args.out / 'metrics.json').write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2) + '\n')
+    print(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2))
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.Code254
+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.DominatedImplication
+
+/-!
+Compatibility adapter for the representation-independent implication theorem.
+The phase-seven DomImp, rho8_all, composition and lift_right interfaces are
+retained. The truth field remains for compatibility; the general theorem
+requires only modus ponens and restricted rows. Source 149 / CD230 ancestry
+and the generic-core proposal e94206c09f supply the inherited derivation.
+-/
+
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.DomRho8
+
+open Code254
+
+/-- Truth, modus ponens and the dominated rho8 instances. -/
+structure DomImp (T : Nat → Prop) : Prop where
+  truth : T 0
+  mp : ∀ {a b : Nat}, T (wim a b) → T a → T b
+  rho8 : ∀ a b c u : Nat, u ≤ a → T (Code254.rho8 a b c u)
+
+theorem le_l {u x : Nat} (y : Nat) (h : u ≤ x) : u ≤ wim x y :=
+  Nat.le_trans h (by have := le_P_left x y; simp only [wim]; omega)
+
+theorem le_r {u y : Nat} (x : Nat) (h : u ≤ y) : u ≤ wim x y :=
+  Nat.le_trans h (by have := le_P_right x y; simp only [wim]; omega)
+
+/-- A substitution: the valuation sending variable `i` to the `i`-th code. -/
+def sub (l : List Nat) (i : Nat) : Nat := l.getD i 0
+
+theorem wim00 : wim 0 0 = 0 := by simp [wim, P, Cantor.toNat, Cantor.tri]
+
+private def language : DominatedImplication.Language Nat where
+  imp := wim
+  below := Nat.le
+  refl := Nat.le_refl
+  grow_left := fun y hu => le_l y hu
+  grow_right := fun x hu => le_r x hu
+
+private theorem restricted {T : Nat → Prop}
+    (mp : ∀ {a b : Nat}, T (wim a b) → T a → T b)
+    (row : ∀ a b c u : Nat, u ≤ a → T (Code254.rho8 a b c u)) :
+    DominatedImplication.Restricted language T where
+  mp := mp
+  rho8 := row
+
+/-- The truth premise is unnecessary for recovering unrestricted rho8. -/
+theorem rho8_all_of_restricted {T : Nat → Prop}
+    (mp : ∀ {a b : Nat}, T (wim a b) → T a → T b)
+    (row : ∀ a b c u : Nat, u ≤ a → T (Code254.rho8 a b c u))
+    (a b c u : Nat) : T (Code254.rho8 a b c u) :=
+  DominatedImplication.rho8_all (restricted mp row) a b c u
+
+section
+variable {T : Nat → Prop} (h : DomImp T)
+include h
+
+theorem composition (a b c : Nat) : T (wim (wim a b) (wim (wim b c) (wim a c))) :=
+  DominatedImplication.composition (restricted h.mp h.rho8) a b c
+
+theorem lift_right {a b : Nat} (hab : T (wim a b)) (x : Nat) :
+    T (wim (wim x a) (wim x b)) :=
+  DominatedImplication.lift_right (restricted h.mp h.rho8) hab x
+
+theorem rho8_all (a b c u : Nat) : T (Code254.rho8 a b c u) :=
+  rho8_all_of_restricted h.mp h.rho8 a b c u
+
+end
+#print axioms rho8_all

+#print axioms rho8_all_of_restricted
+end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.DomRho8

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Own bounded producer reproduction. Requires the independently frozen clean peer."""
+import hashlib,json,pathlib,shutil,subprocess,sys,time
+O=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+FROZEN='1626c437e96a1958f5264e2ca0bf2803c877cbdcbe37d9c789b6c168c50290d8'
+PEER=pathlib.Path('/tmp/k215-upstream49-source-review/producer-review.json')
+def sha(p):return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+def js(p):return json.loads(pathlib.Path(p).read_text())
+def pin(p):return {'path':str(p),'bytes':p.stat().st_size,'sha256':sha(p)}
+assert sha(O/'freeze.json')==FROZEN
+f=js(O/'freeze.json')
+for r in f['files']:assert sha(O/r['path'])==r['sha256']
+# The final independently reviewed receipt path/hash is supplied explicitly.
+assert len(sys.argv)==3,'usage: run_reproduction.py PEER_JSON PEER_SHA256'
+PEER=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]);assert sha(PEER)==sys.argv[2]
+peer=js(PEER);assert 'PASS' in peer['status']
+out=O/'reproduction-run1';out.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
+layout=out/'layout';formal=layout/'Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/k225-formal'
+formal.mkdir(parents=True)
+for p in (O/'production').rglob('*'):
+ if p.is_file():q=formal/p.relative_to(O/'production');q.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);q.write_bytes(p.read_bytes())
+lean=layout/'Computability/BusyBeaver/Lean'
+producer=formal/'generate_dominated_implication_lean.py'
+before={'freeze':pin(O/'freeze.json'),'peer':pin(PEER),'runner':pin(pathlib.Path(__file__)),
+ 'owned_originals':[pin(O/r['path']) for r in f['files']],
+ 'disposable_inputs':[pin(p) for p in sorted(formal.rglob('*')) if p.is_file()]}
+(out/'before.json').write_text(json.dumps(before,indent=2)+'\n')
+jobs=[('controls',[sys.executable,'-B',str(O/'controls.py')]),
+ ('generate',[sys.executable,'-B',str(producer),'--out',str(lean)]),
+ ('explicit-output-check',[sys.executable,'-B',str(producer),'--out',str(lean),'--check']),
+ ('explicit-default-check',[sys.executable,'-B',str(producer),'--check']),
+ ('implicit-default-check',[sys.executable,'-B',str(producer)])]
+records=[];status='PASS'
+for number,(name,cmd) in enumerate(jobs,1):
+ d=out/f'{number:02d}-{name}';d.mkdir();log=d/'stdout.log';start=time.monotonic();timed=False
+ with log.open('wb') as stream:
+  try:r=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=formal,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=30);code=r.returncode
+  except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:code=None;timed=True
+ record={'name':name,'command':cmd,'cwd':str(formal),'timeout_seconds':30,'exit_code':code,'timed_out':timed,'seconds':time.monotonic()-start,'log':pin(log)}
+ (d/'record.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n');records.append(record)
+ if code!=0 or timed:status='FAIL';break
+ parsed=json.loads(log.read_text())
+ if name=='controls':
+  assert parsed['status']=='PASS_OWN_PRODUCER_CONTROLS'
+  assert len([x for x in parsed['results'] if x['kind']=='positive'])==4
+  assert len([x for x in parsed['results'] if x['kind']=='negative'])==15
+ else:
+  assert parsed['generic_sha256']==f['expected_core_sha256']
+  assert parsed['adapter_sha256']==f['expected_adapter_sha256']
+  assert parsed['raw_checked']['private_mp']==58 and parsed['checked']['private_mp']==56
+  assert parsed['raw_checked']['restricted_rows']==parsed['checked']['restricted_rows']==23
+  assert parsed['checked']['public_mp']==3
+for r in before['owned_originals']+before['disposable_inputs']:assert sha(r['path'])==r['sha256']
+assert sha(O/'freeze.json')==FROZEN and sha(PEER)==sys.argv[2]
+outputs=[]
+if status=='PASS':
+ for name,expected in [('DominatedImplication.lean',f['expected_core_sha256']),('DomRho8.lean',f['expected_adapter_sha256'])]:
+  p=lean/'BusyBeaver/ZFC'/name;assert sha(p)==expected;outputs.append(pin(p))
+ assert not (formal/'dominated_implication_templates/core-prefix.txt').exists()
+ assert not (formal/'dominated_implication_templates/core-suffix.txt').exists()
+actual={'status':status,'jobs':records,'outputs':outputs,'all_before_input_bytes_unchanged':True,
+ 'source_freeze_sha256':FROZEN,'peer_sha256':sys.argv[2],'supplied_renderer_executions':0,'compiler_invocations':0,'canonical_writes':0,
+ 'scope':'Own producer/source diagnostic and five CLI/control invocations, no kernel or full endpoint claim.'}
+(out/'actual.json').write_text(json.dumps(actual,indent=2)+'\n')
+print(json.dumps({'status':status,'actual_sha256':sha(out/'actual.json'),'jobs':len(records),'output':str(out)},indent=2))
+raise SystemExit(0 if status=='PASS' else 1)

+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.KThmK
+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.KEqCodes222

+/-!
+Completeness of the 222/221 code calculus, through the equality interpretation.
+
+Port of `k225-formal/rocq224/src/L224E.v`. `Eind x y` says that `x` and `y` have the same
+members and belong to the same sets (auxiliary bound name `aux x y = x + y + 1`), and `th`
+replaces every equality atom by `Eind`. Each rule of the Tarski calculus `Thm` interprets in
+`ThmK`, which has equality vacuity only at the helper binder (`thm_th`); the five equality rows
+become the lemmas `Eind_ex`, `Eind_euclid`, `Eind_el_l`, `Eind_el_r`, `Eind_vac`. Every rule
+of `ThmK` is a derivation in the code calculus `C222` (`c222_of_thmK`). With Tarski's
+completeness theorem this gives `c222_complete`: if a set of named formulas whose interpreted
+codes are derivable has no irreflexive model, the code 1 is derivable.
+-/
+
+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KEind222
+
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Tarski (NF Thm rn rv complete h0 h1 h2 ded1 ded2 syl dne all_mono ex_mono)
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Tarski.NF Kalmar SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KThmK
+
+/-! ## The interpretation -/
+
+def wa (a b : NF) : NF := neg (imp a (neg b))
+def biff (a b : NF) : NF := wa (imp a b) (imp b a)
+def Bin (v x y : Nat) : NF := biff (rel v x) (rel v y)
+def Bout (v x y : Nat) : NF := biff (rel x v) (rel y v)
+def Ev (v x y : Nat) : NF := wa (all v (Bin v x y)) (all v (Bout v x y))
+def aux (x y : Nat) : Nat := x + y + 1
+def Eind (x y : Nat) : NF := Ev (aux x y) x y
+
+def th : NF → NF
+  | rel i j => rel i j
+  | NF.eq i j => Eind i j
+  | NF.bot => NF.bot
+  | imp a b => imp (th a) (th b)
+  | all i a => all i (th a)
+
+variable {Ax : NF → Prop}
+
+/-! ## Conjunction -/
+
+theorem and_intro (A B : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp A (imp B (wa A B))) := by
+  apply ded2 classical
+  apply deduction classical
+  -- [A → ¬B, B, A] ⊢ ⊥
+  exact .mp (.mp h0 h2) h1
+
+theorem and_l (A B : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp (wa A B) A) := by
+  apply syl classical _ (dne classical A)
+  apply ded1 classical
+  apply deduction classical
+  -- [¬A, wa A B] ⊢ ⊥
+  have hn : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [neg A, wa A B] (imp A (neg B)) := by
+    apply deduction classical
+    exact .mp (.ax (ex_falso (neg B))) (.mp h1 h0)
+  exact .mp h1 hn
+
+theorem and_r (A B : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp (wa A B) B) := by
+  apply syl classical _ (dne classical B)
+  apply ded1 classical
+  apply deduction classical
+  have hn : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [neg B, wa A B] (imp A (neg B)) := by
+    apply deduction classical
+    exact h1
+  exact .mp h1 hn
+
+/-! ## Syntax facts -/
+
+theorem qf_bin (v x y : Nat) : QF (Bin v x y) := by simp [Bin, biff, wa, neg, QF]
+theorem qf_bout (v x y : Nat) : QF (Bout v x y) := by simp [Bout, biff, wa, neg, QF]
+theorem ef_bin (v x y : Nat) : EqFree (Bin v x y) := by simp [Bin, biff, wa, neg, EqFree]
+theorem ef_bout (v x y : Nat) : EqFree (Bout v x y) := by simp [Bout, biff, wa, neg, EqFree]
+theorem ef_ev (v x y : Nat) : EqFree (Ev v x y) := by
+  simp [Ev, wa, neg, EqFree, Bin, Bout, biff]
+
+theorem rn_bin {v w x y : Nat} (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) : rn v w (Bin v x y) = Bin w x y := by
+  simp [Bin, biff, wa, neg, rn, rv, hx, hy]
+theorem rn_bout {v w x y : Nat} (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) : rn v w (Bout v x y) = Bout w x y := by
+  simp [Bout, biff, wa, neg, rn, rv, hx, hy]
+
+theorem occ_bin {n v x y : Nat} (hv : n ≠ v) (hx : n ≠ x) (hy : n ≠ y) : ¬ Occurs n (Bin v x y) := by
+  simp [Bin, biff, wa, neg, Occurs]; omega
+theorem occ_bout {n v x y : Nat} (hv : n ≠ v) (hx : n ≠ x) (hy : n ≠ y) : ¬ Occurs n (Bout v x y) := by
+  simp [Bout, biff, wa, neg, Occurs]; omega
+theorem occ_ev {n v x y : Nat} (hv : n ≠ v) (hx : n ≠ x) (hy : n ≠ y) : ¬ Occurs n (Ev v x y) := by
+  simp [Ev, Bin, Bout, biff, wa, neg, Occurs]; omega
+
+/-! ## Renaming the auxiliary label -/
+
+theorem all_bin_alpha {v w x y : Nat} (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) (hwx : w ≠ x) (hwy : w ≠ y) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (all v (Bin v x y)) (all w (Bin w x y))) := by
+  by_cases hvw : w = v
+  · subst hvw; exact classical.mp (classical.mp (classical.s _ _ _) (classical.k _ _))
+      (classical.k _ (all w (Bin w x y)))
+  · have h := alpha_fwd (Ax := Ax) hvw (qf_bin v x y) (ef_bin v x y)
+      (occ_bin hvw hwx hwy)
+    rwa [rn_bin hx hy] at h
+
+theorem all_bout_alpha {v w x y : Nat} (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) (hwx : w ≠ x) (hwy : w ≠ y) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (all v (Bout v x y)) (all w (Bout w x y))) := by
+  by_cases hvw : w = v
+  · subst hvw; exact classical.mp (classical.mp (classical.s _ _ _) (classical.k _ _))
+      (classical.k _ (all w (Bout w x y)))
+  · have h := alpha_fwd (Ax := Ax) hvw (qf_bout v x y) (ef_bout v x y)
+      (occ_bout hvw hwx hwy)
+    rwa [rn_bout hx hy] at h
+
+/-- `Ev v x y → Ev w x y` for labels outside `{x, y}`. -/
+theorem ev_alpha {v w x y : Nat} (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) (hwx : w ≠ x) (hwy : w ≠ y) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (Ev v x y) (Ev w x y)) := by
+  apply ded1 classical
+  have hin : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Ev v x y] (all w (Bin w x y)) :=
+    .mp (.ax (all_bin_alpha hx hy hwx hwy)) (.mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) h0)
+  have hout : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Ev v x y] (all w (Bout w x y)) :=
+    .mp (.ax (all_bout_alpha hx hy hwx hwy)) (.mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) h0)
+  exact .mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) hin) hout
+
+theorem aux_ne_l (x y : Nat) : x ≠ aux x y := by simp [aux]; omega
+theorem aux_ne_r (x y : Nat) : y ≠ aux x y := by simp [aux]; omega
+
+theorem eind_to {w x y : Nat} (hwx : w ≠ x) (hwy : w ≠ y) : ThmK Ax (imp (Eind x y) (Ev w x y)) :=
+  ev_alpha (aux_ne_l x y) (aux_ne_r x y) hwx hwy
+
+theorem eind_of {w x y : Nat} (hwx : w ≠ x) (hwy : w ≠ y) : ThmK Ax (imp (Ev w x y) (Eind x y)) :=
+  ev_alpha (Ne.symm hwx) (Ne.symm hwy) (Ne.symm (aux_ne_l x y)) (Ne.symm (aux_ne_r x y))
+
+/-! ## Specialization of the indiscernibility clauses -/
+
+theorem bin_spec {v x y c : Nat} (hcv : c ≠ v) (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (all v (Bin v x y)) (biff (rel c x) (rel c y))) := by
+  have h := spec (Ax := Ax) hcv (qf_bin v x y) (ef_bin v x y)
+  have e : rn v c (Bin v x y) = biff (rel c x) (rel c y) := by
+    simp [Bin, biff, wa, neg, rn, rv, hx, hy]
+  rwa [e] at h
+
+theorem bout_spec {v x y c : Nat} (hcv : c ≠ v) (hx : x ≠ v) (hy : y ≠ v) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (all v (Bout v x y)) (biff (rel x c) (rel y c))) := by
+  have h := spec (Ax := Ax) hcv (qf_bout v x y) (ef_bout v x y)
+  have e : rn v c (Bout v x y) = biff (rel x c) (rel y c) := by
+    simp [Bout, biff, wa, neg, rn, rv, hx, hy]
+  rwa [e] at h
+
+/-- A label different from three given ones. -/
+def fresh3 (a b c : Nat) : Nat := a + b + c + 1
+
+theorem fresh3_ne (a b c : Nat) : fresh3 a b c ≠ a ∧ fresh3 a b c ≠ b ∧ fresh3 a b c ≠ c := by
+  simp [fresh3]; omega
+
+/-- th(rho3): `Eind a b → (c ∈ a → c ∈ b)`. -/
+theorem Eind_el_r (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (Eind a b) (imp (rel c a) (rel c b))) := by
+  obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := fresh3_ne a b c
+  have t := eind_to (Ax := Ax) h1 h2
+  have s := bin_spec (Ax := Ax) (v := fresh3 a b c) (x := a) (y := b) (c := c) (Ne.symm h3)
+    (Ne.symm h1) (Ne.symm h2)
+  apply ded1 classical
+  have hev : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind a b] (Ev (fresh3 a b c) a b) := .mp (.ax t) h0
+  have hb : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind a b] (biff (rel c a) (rel c b)) :=
+    .mp (.ax s) (.mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) hev)
+  exact .mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) hb
+
+/-- th(rho5): `Eind c a → (c ∈ b → a ∈ b)`. -/
+theorem Eind_el_l (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (Eind c a) (imp (rel c b) (rel a b))) := by
+  obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := fresh3_ne c a b
+  have t := eind_to (Ax := Ax) h1 h2
+  have s := bout_spec (Ax := Ax) (v := fresh3 c a b) (x := c) (y := a) (c := b) (Ne.symm h3)
+    (Ne.symm h1) (Ne.symm h2)
+  apply ded1 classical
+  have hev : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind c a] (Ev (fresh3 c a b) c a) := .mp (.ax t) h0
+  have hb : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind c a] (biff (rel c b) (rel a b)) :=
+    .mp (.ax s) (.mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) hev)
+  exact .mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) hb
+
+/-! ## Euclid and existence -/
+
+/-- `(p ↔ q) → (p ↔ r) → (q ↔ r)`, propositionally. -/
+theorem biff_euclid (p q r : NF) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (biff p q) (imp (biff p r) (biff q r))) := by
+  apply ded2 classical
+  have pq : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp p q) := .mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) h1
+  have qp : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp q p) := .mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) h1
+  have pr : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp p r) := .mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) h0
+  have rp : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp r p) := .mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) h0
+  have qr : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp q r) := by
+    apply deduction classical
+    exact .mp pr.weaken (.mp qp.weaken h0)
+  have rq : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [biff p r, biff p q] (imp r q) := by
+    apply deduction classical
+    exact .mp pq.weaken (.mp rp.weaken h0)
+  exact .mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) qr) rq
+
+/-- Distribution of a two-premise implication under `∀`. -/
+theorem all_mono2 (i : Nat) {a b c : NF} (h : ThmK Ax (imp a (imp b c))) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (all i a) (imp (all i b) (all i c))) :=
+  syl classical (all_mono classical i h) (.rho2 i b c)
+
+theorem ev_euclid (v x y z : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (Ev v x y) (imp (Ev v x z) (Ev v y z))) := by
+  have hin := all_mono2 (Ax := Ax) v (biff_euclid (rel v x) (rel v y) (rel v z))
+  have hout := all_mono2 (Ax := Ax) v (biff_euclid (rel x v) (rel y v) (rel z v))
+  apply ded2 classical
+  have i1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Ev v x z, Ev v x y] (all v (Bin v y z)) :=
+    .mp (.mp (.ax hin) (.mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) h1)) (.mp (.ax (and_l _ _)) h0)
+  have o1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Ev v x z, Ev v x y] (all v (Bout v y z)) :=
+    .mp (.mp (.ax hout) (.mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) h1)) (.mp (.ax (and_r _ _)) h0)
+  exact .mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) i1) o1
+
+/-- th(rho7): `Eind c a → (Eind c b → Eind a b)`. -/
+theorem Eind_euclid (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (Eind c a) (imp (Eind c b) (Eind a b))) := by
+  let w := fresh3 a b c
+  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc⟩ := fresh3_ne a b c
+  have e := ev_euclid (Ax := Ax) w c a b
+  apply ded2 classical
+  have x1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind c b, Eind c a] (Ev w c a) := .mp (.ax (eind_to hc ha)) h1
+  have x2 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [Eind c b, Eind c a] (Ev w c b) := .mp (.ax (eind_to hc hb)) h0
+  exact .mp (.ax (eind_of ha hb)) (.mp (.mp (.ax e) x1) x2)
+
+/-- `x = y → Eind x y`, through the helper binder. -/
+theorem Eq_Eind (x y : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (Eind x y)) := by
+  let w := Code254.wel x y
+  have hwx : w ≠ x := Ne.symm (Nat.ne_of_lt (KCode222.lt_wel_left x y))
+  have hwy : w ≠ y := Ne.symm (Nat.ne_of_lt (KCode222.lt_wel_right x y))
+  -- x = y → (w ∈ x ↔ w ∈ y) and → (x ∈ w ↔ y ∈ w)
+  have bi : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (Bin w x y)) := by
+    apply ded1 classical
+    have f1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (imp (rel w x) (rel w y)) := .mp (.ax (.rho3 x y w)) h0
+    have f2 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (imp (rel w y) (rel w x)) :=
+      .mp (.ax (.rho3 y x w)) (.mp (.ax (eq_symm x y)) h0)
+    exact .mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) f1) f2
+  have bo : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (Bout w x y)) := by
+    apply ded1 classical
+    have f1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (imp (rel x w) (rel y w)) := .mp (.ax (.rho5 y w x)) h0
+    have f2 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (imp (rel y w) (rel x w)) :=
+      .mp (.ax (.rho5 x w y)) (.mp (.ax (eq_symm x y)) h0)
+    exact .mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) f1) f2
+  apply ded1 classical
+  have hall : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (all w (NF.eq x y)) := .mp (.ax (.helper x y)) h0
+  have i1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (all w (Bin w x y)) := .mp (.ax (all_mono classical w bi)) hall
+  have o1 : Der NF.imp (ThmK Ax) [NF.eq x y] (all w (Bout w x y)) := .mp (.ax (all_mono classical w bo)) hall
+  exact .mp (.ax (eind_of hwx hwy)) (.mp (.mp (.ax (and_intro _ _)) i1) o1)
+
+/-- th(rho1): `∃i Eind(i, j)`. -/
+theorem Eind_ex (i j : Nat) : ThmK Ax (ex i (Eind i j)) :=
+  ThmK.mp (ex_mono classical i (Eq_Eind i j)) (.rho1 i j)
+
+/-- th(vacEq): `Eind a b → ∀c Eind a b` for `c ≠ a, b`. -/
+theorem Eind_vac (a b c : Nat) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (Eind a b) (all c (Eind a b))) := by
+  by_cases hc : c = aux a b
+  · let w := fresh3 a b c
+    obtain ⟨ha, hb, hwc⟩ := fresh3_ne a b c
+    have v : ThmK Ax (imp (Ev w a b) (all c (Ev w a b))) :=
+      vac_of_not_occurs c _ (ef_ev w a b) (occ_ev (Ne.symm hwc) hca hcb)
+    exact syl classical (syl classical (eind_to ha hb) v) (all_mono classical c (eind_of ha hb))
+  · exact vac_of_not_occurs c _ (ef_ev _ a b) (occ_ev hc hca hcb)
+
+/-! ## The interpretation of derivations -/
+
+theorem th_neg (a : NF) : th (neg a) = neg (th a) := rfl
+theorem th_ex (i : Nat) (a : NF) : th (ex i a) = ex i (th a) := rfl
+theorem th_luk (c u a b : NF) : th (luk c u a b) = luk (th c) (th u) (th a) (th b) := rfl
+
+theorem thm_th {f : NF} (h : Thm Ax f) : ThmK (fun g => ∃ a, Ax a ∧ th a = g) (th f) := by
+  induction h with
+  | ax h => exact .ax ⟨_, h, rfl⟩
+  | mp _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact .mp ih1 ih2
+  | gen i _ ih => exact .gen i ih
+  | rho8 c u a b => exact .rho8 (th c) (th u) (th a) (th b)
+  | rho2 i b c => exact .rho2 i (th b) (th c)
+  | rho4 i j c => exact .rho4 i j (th c)
+  | rho6 i b => exact .rho6 i (th b)
+  | rho1 i j => exact Eind_ex i j
+  | rho7 a b c => exact Eind_euclid a b c
+  | rho5 a b c => exact Eind_el_l a b c
+  | rho3 a b c => exact Eind_el_r a b c
+  | vacRel a b c h1 h2 => exact .vacRel a b c h1 h2
+  | vacEq a b c h1 h2 => exact Eind_vac a b c h1 h2
+
+/-! ## Into the code calculus -/
+
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Code254 SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KCode222
+  SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KEqCodes222

+theorem c222_of_thmK {T : NF → Prop} (hT : ∀ f, T f → C222 (enc f)) {f : NF}
+    (h : ThmK T f) : C222 (enc f) := by
+  induction h with
+  | ax h => exact hT _ h
+  | mp _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact C222.mp ih2 ih1
+  | gen i _ ih => exact C222.gen i ih
+  | rho8 c u a b => exact C222.r8 (enc a) (enc b) (enc c) (enc u)
+  | rho2 i b c => exact C222.r2 i (enc b) (enc c)
+  | rho4 i j c => exact C222.r4 i j (enc c)
+  | rho6 i b => exact C222.r6 i (enc b)
+  | rho1 i j => exact C222.r1 i j
+  | rho7 a b c => exact rho7_222 a b c
+  | rho5 a b c => exact C222.r5 a b c
+  | rho3 a b c => exact C222.r3 a b c
+  | vacRel a b c h1 h2 => exact vrel_of_bundle a b c h1 h2
+  | helper a b => exact helper222 a b
+
+/-- Irreflexivity, as a named sentence. -/
+def irNF : NF := all 0 (neg (rel 0 0))
+
+/-- **Completeness.** If the named formulas of `T`, whose interpreted codes are derivable, have
+no irreflexive model with a valuation, then the code 1 is derivable. -/
+theorem c222_complete (T : NF → Prop) (hT : ∀ f, T f → C222 (enc (th f)))
+    (hnone : ∀ (D : Type) (mem : D → D → Prop), (∀ x, ¬ mem x x) →
+      (∀ f, T f → ∀ e : Nat → D, Tarski.Sat mem e f) → (Nat → D) → False) :
+    C222 F := by
+  let Ax : NF → Prop := fun f => T f ∨ f = irNF
+  have hbot : Thm Ax NF.bot := by
+    apply complete
+    intro D mem hAx e
+    have hirr : ∀ x, ¬ mem x x := by
+      intro x hx
+      have := hAx irNF (Or.inr rfl) e x
+      exact this hx
+    exact (hnone D mem hirr (fun f hf => hAx f (Or.inl hf)) e).elim
+  have hK := thm_th hbot
+  have := c222_of_thmK (T := fun g => ∃ a, Ax a ∧ th a = g) (by
+    rintro g ⟨a, ha | rfl, rfl⟩
+    · exact hT a ha
+    · show C222 (wal 0 (wim (wel 0 0) F))
+      rw [wel_zero_zero]
+      exact C222.gen 0 (self_imp c222_classical F)) hK
+  simpa [th, enc] using this
+
+#print axioms c222_complete
+
+end SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KEind222

+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.TarskiLeibniz
+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.Lukasiewicz
+import BusyBeaver.ZFC.Code254

+/-!
+`ThmK`: the named calculus that the 222/221 code calculus simulates.
+
+It is the Tarski calculus `Thm` with one change: equality vacuity is available only at the
+helper binder, `Eq(a,b) → ∀_{wel a b} Eq(a,b)` (the merged row G gives exactly this, and rho7;
+`KEqCodes222`). Membership vacuity stays at every fresh binder.
+
+The derived rules of `TarskiDerived` and `TarskiLeibniz` that do not use equality vacuity
+apply to `ThmK` directly (its `classical` basis and `Rows` instance). The rest are re-proved
+here where `Thm` used equality vacuity at an arbitrary binder:
+
+* `vac_of_not_occurs` and `ex_elim` are stated for equality-free formulas;
+* Leibniz's law, specialization and alpha-renaming are stated for quantifier-free,

+namespace SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.KThmK

+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.Tarski NF Kalmar

+inductive ThmK (Ax : NF → Prop) : NF → Prop
+  | ax {a : NF} : Ax a → ThmK Ax a
+  | mp {a b : NF} : ThmK Ax (imp a b) → ThmK Ax a → ThmK Ax b
+  | gen (i : Nat) {a : NF} : ThmK Ax a → ThmK Ax (all i a)
+  | rho8 (c u a b : NF) : ThmK Ax (luk c u a b)
+  | rho2 (i : Nat) (b c : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp (all i (imp b c)) (imp (all i b) (all i c)))
+  | rho4 (i j : Nat) (c : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp (all i (all j c)) (all j (all i c)))
+  | rho6 (i : Nat) (b : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp (ex i (all i b)) b)
+  | rho1 (i j : Nat) : ThmK Ax (ex i (NF.eq i j))
+  | rho7 (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq c a) (imp (NF.eq c b) (NF.eq a b)))
+  | rho5 (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq c a) (imp (rel c b) (rel a b)))
+  | rho3 (a b c : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq a b) (imp (rel c a) (rel c b)))
+  | vacRel (a b c : Nat) : c ≠ a → c ≠ b → ThmK Ax (imp (rel a b) (all c (rel a b)))
+  | helper (a b : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq a b) (all (Code254.wel a b) (NF.eq a b)))
+
+/-! ## Syntactic classes -/
+
+def EqFree : NF → Prop
+  | rel _ _ => True
+  | NF.eq _ _ => False
+  | NF.bot => True
+  | imp a b => EqFree a ∧ EqFree b
+  | all _ a => EqFree a
+
+def QF : NF → Prop
+  | all _ _ => False
+  | imp a b => QF a ∧ QF b
+  | _ => True
+
+theorem eqFree_rn (x y : Nat) : ∀ f : NF, EqFree f → EqFree (rn x y f)
+  | rel _ _, _ => trivial
+  | NF.eq _ _, h => h.elim
+  | NF.bot, _ => trivial
+  | imp a b, h => ⟨eqFree_rn x y a h.1, eqFree_rn x y b h.2⟩
+  | all i a, h => by
+      by_cases hi : i = x
+      · simp only [rn, hi, if_true]; exact h
+      · simp only [rn, hi, if_false]; exact eqFree_rn x y a h
+
+variable {Ax : NF → Prop}
+
+/-! ## Classical basis -/
+
+theorem implicational : Lukasiewicz.Implicational NF.imp (ThmK Ax) where
+  mp := ThmK.mp
+  rho8 := ThmK.rho8
+
+theorem ex_falso (a : NF) : ThmK Ax (imp bot a) := by
+  let x := all 0 (neg (all 0 a))
+  let e := ex 0 (all 0 a)
+  have hk := Lukasiewicz.k (implicational (Ax := Ax))
+  have hs := Lukasiewicz.s (implicational (Ax := Ax))
+  have hbe : ThmK Ax (imp bot e) := hk bot x
+  have hbea : ThmK Ax (imp bot (imp e a)) :=
+    .mp (hk (imp e a) bot) (.rho6 0 a)
+  exact .mp (.mp (hs bot e a) hbea) hbe
+
+theorem classical : Classical NF.imp NF.bot (ThmK Ax) where
+  mp := ThmK.mp
+  k := Lukasiewicz.k implicational
+  s := Lukasiewicz.s implicational
+  peirce := Lukasiewicz.peirce implicational
+  efq := ex_falso
+
+/-- The rows shared with `Thm`: the propositional and quantifier rules of `TarskiDerived`
+and `TarskiLeibniz` apply to `ThmK` through `classical` and this instance. -/
+instance : Rows (ThmK Ax) where
+  gen := .gen
+  rho2 := .rho2
+  rho4 := .rho4
+  rho6 := .rho6
+  rho1 := .rho1
+  rho7 := .rho7
+  rho5 := .rho5
+  rho3 := .rho3
+  vacRel := .vacRel

+/-! ## Vacuity and equality at the helper binder -/
+
+/-- Vacuity for every equality-free formula not containing the label. -/
+theorem vac_of_not_occurs (i : Nat) :
+    ∀ f : NF, EqFree f → ¬ Occurs i f → ThmK Ax (imp f (all i f))
+  | rel a b, _, h => .vacRel a b i (fun e => h (Or.inl e)) (fun e => h (Or.inr e))
+  | NF.eq _ _, hf, _ => hf.elim
+  | NF.bot, _, _ => ex_falso _
+  | imp a b, hf, h => vac_imp classical (vac_of_not_occurs i a hf.1 (fun o => h (Or.inl o)))
+      (vac_of_not_occurs i b hf.2 (fun o => h (Or.inr o)))
+  | all _ a, hf, h => vac_all classical (vac_of_not_occurs i a hf (fun o => h (Or.inr o)))
+
+theorem ex_elim (i : Nat) {a : NF} (hf : EqFree a) (h : ¬ Occurs i a) :
+    ThmK Ax (imp (ex i a) a) :=
+  ex_elim_of_vac classical (vac_of_not_occurs i a hf h)
+
+theorem eq_refl (x : Nat) : ThmK Ax (NF.eq x x) := by
+  have h7 : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq (Code254.wel x x) x) (NF.eq x x)) := by
+    have r : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq (Code254.wel x x) x)
+        (imp (NF.eq (Code254.wel x x) x) (NF.eq x x))) := .rho7 x x (Code254.wel x x)
+    exact ded1 classical (.mp (.mp (.ax r) h0) h0)
+  have hex : ThmK Ax (ex (Code254.wel x x) (NF.eq x x)) :=
+    ThmK.mp (ex_mono classical (Code254.wel x x) h7) (.rho1 (Code254.wel x x) x)
+  exact ThmK.mp (ex_elim_of_vac classical (.helper x x)) hex
+
+theorem eq_symm (x y : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (NF.eq y x)) :=
+  ded1 classical (.mp (.mp (.ax (.rho7 y x x)) h0) (.ax (eq_refl x)))
+
+theorem eq_trans (x y z : Nat) : ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (imp (NF.eq y z) (NF.eq x z))) := by
+  apply ded2 classical
+  exact .mp (.mp (.ax (.rho7 x z y)) (.mp (.ax (eq_symm x y)) h1)) h0
+
+/-! ## Leibniz's law for quantifier-free membership formulas -/
+
+/-- Leibniz's law for quantifier-free, equality-free formulas. -/
+theorem leibniz (x y : Nat) :
+    ∀ f : NF, QF f → EqFree f →
+      ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (imp f (rn x y f))) ∧
+      ThmK Ax (imp (NF.eq x y) (imp (rn x y f) f))
